post.caption: Purple sugilite hid inside manganese ore. It is named for Sugi, who found it in Japan in 1944. Those tiny Japanese crystals were too small for jewelry. Rich purple gem sugilite came from the Wessels mine in South Africa. It turned up in a mine that was digging for manganese. At first, the purple rock was overlooked as mine waste. Dealers saw its worth, and it reached the gem market in 1979. Dealers sold it as Royal Azel and Royal Lavulite. One more trade name, wesselite, honors the mine. Most gem sugilite is cut as smooth domes called cabochons. The purple color comes from manganese.
